label: Ātma-Nivedana Song Six
title: bastutaḥ sakali tava jīva keho no
incipit: bastutaḥ sakali tava, jīva keho noy
metaDescription: Ātma-Nivedana Song Six: (bastutaḥ sakali tava jīva keho no) of Śaraṇāgati (‘Surrender’) written by Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in 1893. This songbook contains 50 songs detailing the six symptoms of surrender unto the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

translit: bastutaḥ sakali tava, jīva keho noy
verses.translation: In truth, all things belong to You; no jīva is ever the owner of anything. The tiny soul wanders in this world mistakenly thinking in terms of aham (“I am this material body and mind”), and mama (“everything related to this body is mine”). Thus he suffers the consequences of both sorrow and fear.

translit: baddha-jīva nija boli’ jāne mane man
verses.translation: The conditioned soul thinks that all the things related to the false conceptions of “I” and “mine” are his exclusive treasures. Calling them his own, his mind is firmly convinced of this gross delusion.
Due to such vanity, I also fell into this material world. Floundering in the ocean of mundane existence like a drowning man, I suffer the pangs of rising and sinking in that ocean.
I take shelter at Your lotus feet, which deliver one from fear, and dedicate the whole of myself to You on this day.

translit: ār jeno mama hṛde stāna nāhi pāy
verses.translation: The false conception of thinking in terms of “I” and “mine” has left me now. May it never again find a place to settle within my heart.

translit: ei mātro bala prabhu! dibe he āmāre
verses.translation: Please give me this strength alone, O Lord, that I may be able to keep the false conceptions of “I” and “mine” far away.

translit: hasti-snāna sama jeno khanika nā hoy
verses.translation: May the mood of self-surrender to You remain firmly fixed in my heart and not prove to be momentary like the cleanliness of an elephant after a bath.
